result:
`pricebook.py` had 11 rules whose behavior didn't match their docstrings or the shared rules in the module docstring. I fixed all of them to follow the docstrings.

I wrote a check that turns each of the 150 docstrings into the correct result and compares it with the actual function. It covers every quantity from 0 up to 5× the threshold plus 1,000, 5,000 and 20,000 units, against 13 unit prices. Before the fixes it found 11 mismatches; after them it finds none.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | Capped the price before taking the percentage, not the discount itself | Compute the discount, then cap it at 30,000 won |
| 15, 124 | Marked "whole" but discounted only the units above the threshold | Discount on the full amount (`base * pct // 100`) |
| 27 | Threshold was 101 instead of 100 | `qty >= 100` |
| 106, 107 | Used `>` so the threshold quantity itself got no discount | Changed to `>=` |
| 40, 55 | Cap only applied once the discount passed double the cap (60,000 / 200,000) | Always apply the cap |
| 46 | Used 4% instead of 3% | 3% |
| 59 | Used 3% instead of 2% | 2% |
| 47 | Rounded with `round()` instead of rounding down to the won | `base * 2 // 100` |

Rule 136 also uses `qty > 5`, but it's a "marginal" rule, so the discount at exactly 5 units is 0 either way and the result is the same. I left it as is. Rules 62 and 144 are written differently from the rest but compute the same thing, so I didn't change them either.

STATUS: DONE
